section.title: Installing virtualization components
section.para: Depending on your deployment requirements, you can choose between two virtualization software patterns:

listitem.para: Installs a minimal-footprint &kvm; virtualization stack (&qemu; and core &libvirt; daemons) without graphical or interactive management utilities such as virt-manager or virt-viewer. This pattern is recommended for headless production servers managed remotely or via automation.
Installs the base &kvm; stack together with the full suite of &libvirt; management and graphical client utilities, including virsh, virt-install, virt-manager and virt-viewer.

section.para: You can install the virtualization components required to run a &vmhost; either when installing the system (see the manual installation), or from an already installed system by installing one of the virtualization patterns.

section.title: Installing patterns during system installation
section.para: During system installation, the virtualization patterns can be selected from the Installation > Software > Patterns selection page. Choose either KVM Host Server pattern under Server Functions, or KVM Virtualization Host and tools under Base Technologies.

section.title: Enable nested virtualization in &kvm;

important.title: Technology preview
important.para: Nested virtualization in &kvm; is still a technology preview. It is provided for testing purposes and is not supported.

section.para: Nested guests are &kvm; guests run in a &kvm; guest. This section describes nested guests using the following virtualization layers:

listitem.para: A virtual machine running on L0. Because it can run another &kvm;, it is called a guest hypervisor.
A virtual machine running on L1. It is called a nested guest.

section.para: Nested virtualization has many advantages. You can benefit from it in the following scenarios:

listitem.para: Manage your own virtual machines directly with your hypervisor of choice in cloud environments.
Enable the live migration of hypervisors and their guest virtual machines as a single entity.

note.para: Live migration of a nested &vmguest; is not supported.

listitem.para: Use it for software development and testing.
